text: Which platform was GSE309890 run on, and what organism is it?

Abstract
This report answers which platform GSE309890 was run on and which organism it studies, using GEO metadata queries. I retrieved the GEO Series record for GSE309890 (geo_series with accession=GSE309890, list_files=false) and resolved the platform accession (geo_resolve_accession with accessions=GPL24659). From the GSE record I extracted: platform = GPL24659, organism (taxon) = "Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655", sample_count = 6, and the GEO series page URL and FTP directory URL. From the platform resolution I obtained the platform GEO page URL. Key results: platform accession GPL24659 (GEO platform page: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659) and organism Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 (GEO series page: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890). These metadata indicate the experiment is RNA expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing on E. coli (6 samples). This matters for data re-use, as it directs where to fetch raw/processed files (GEO FTP) and informs organism-specific downstream analyses.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE accessions in NCBI GEO label expression studies; platform accessions (GPL...) identify the sequencing or array platform. Knowing platform and organism is necessary to select appropriate processing pipelines and reference genomes.
Literature Review. The GEO Series metadata retrieved: title, summary, taxon, experiment_type, platform, sample_count, and FTP directory. No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record as reported in the metadata.
Knowledge Gap. Before querying GEO, the platform accession and exact organism string for GSE309890 were not known to this session.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine the platform accession used for GSE309890 and the organism studied. Hypothesis: the GEO Series metadata will list a platform accession and organism taxon string.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. Query GEO for the Series record, extract platform and taxon, then resolve the platform accession to obtain the platform GEO page URL.
Materials. Databases and tools used:
- NCBI GEO Series metadata via the geo_series tool (functions.geo_series).
- GEO platform resolution via geo_resolve_accession (functions.geo_resolve_accession).
Procedures. Tool calls executed in order (arguments shown exactly as used):
1) functions.geo_series called with {"accession":"GSE309890","list_files":false}. This returned the Series metadata including "platform": "GPL24659" and "taxon": "Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655", sample_count: 6, geo_url and ftp_directory_url.
2) functions.geo_resolve_accession called with {"accessions":"GPL24659"}. This returned the GPL24659 platform UID, ftp_directory_url and geo_url.
Statistical Analysis. No statistical modeling was performed. Reported numeric values are taken directly from fields in the geo_series output: sample_count (denominator = 1 Series record) = 6.

III. Results
Table 1. Key metadata retrieved for GSE309890

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| GSE accession | GSE309890 |
| Series GEO page (provenance) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 |
| Platform accession (as listed in Series) | GPL24659 |
| Platform GEO page (provenance) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659 |
| Organism (taxon string) | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Sample count (as reported) | 6 |
| GEO FTP directory (provenance) | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ |

Findings. The Series GSE309890 was run on platform GPL24659. The organism studied is Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The Series reports 6 samples and an experiment type of high-throughput sequencing.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The GEO metadata directly answers the objective: platform = GPL24659 and organism = Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The sample_count = 6 indicates a small sequencing experiment suitable for E. coli-specific analyses.
Context. The Series metadata includes a title and an extended summary describing experiments in E. coli; no PubMed record is linked to the GEO entry, as stated in the metadata. The GEO FTP directory URL was provided for file download.
Limitations. GEO’s API returned metadata only (the geo_series response notes that processed expression values are not included in the metadata call and must be downloaded from supplementary files on the FTP). The platform resolution returned only the platform accession and GEO page URL — the platform record itself may contain additional details (library layout, instrument model) that were not retrieved here. The absence of a linked PubMed entry means no curated publication metadata was available via this query.
Conclusion & Future Directions. The platform accession for GSE309890 is GPL24659 and the organism is Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. Next useful queries: fetch the GPL24659 platform record to obtain platform details (e.g., instrument/model), and list/download supplementary files from the GEO FTP directory to access raw/processed data for analysis.

References
[1] NCBI GEO — GSE309890 Series page (provenance): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO — GSE309890 FTP directory (provenance): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO — GPL24659 Platform page (provenance): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659
[4] NCBI E-utilities API call used in metadata retrieval (provenance): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

Acknowledgments
NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) for the Series and Platform metadata retrieved via the GEO API calls (geo_series and geo_resolve_accession).
